ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Hong Kong SAR: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615) ('AMLO'); Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) sections 653O-653ZL establishing the Significant Controllers Register ('SCR'); Hong Kong Monetary Authority ('HKMA') Guideline on Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Financing of Terrorism; Counter-Terrorism and Proceeds of Crime Ordinance (Cap. 455); UN Sanctions Ordinance (Cap. 537). People's Republic of China mainland leg: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (2024 revision); Administrative Measures for Anti-Money Laundering and Anti-Terrorist Financing Customer Due Diligence and Customer Identity Data and Transaction Records Preservation (PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3, effective 1 November 2024); Measures for the Record-Filing of Beneficial Owners of Market Entities (SAMR Order No. 86). For any mainland WFOE or EJV leg, the UBO disclosure level is strictly Government_Only_Access; the beneficial owner record is filed with SAMR through the Beneficial Owner Filing system and is not publicly searchable.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong Companies Registrar; for mainland JV leg, State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) or local Administration for Market Regulation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: Notarize the certified true copy before a Hong Kong Notary Public, then obtain an Apostille from the High Court of the Hong Kong SAR (Deputy Registrar, Probate and Formalities Division); no consular step for any state party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention. Consular Legalization path for non-Apostille destination: Notarize before Hong Kong Notary Public, authenticate at Hong Kong High Court, then consular-legalize at the consular post of the destination jurisdiction in Hong Kong or through the Office of the Commissioner of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the PRC in the Hong Kong SAR; never combine the two paths sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Current Status)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong Companies Registry (Register of Companies)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: Verify the current status certificate at the Hong Kong Companies Registry, notarize it under notarial cover, and apply to the High Court of the Hong Kong SAR for an Apostille. Consular Legalization: After Hong Kong notarization and High Court authentication, submit the document to the destination state's consular authority for legalization; do not apply both an Apostille and a consular legalization to the same document.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for Pre-Incorporation and Banking Matters
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Proposed directors of the JV entity, executed before a notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: Execute the resolution and power of attorney before a Hong Kong Notary Public, then have the High Court Registry issue an Apostille. Consular Legalization: Execute before a notary, obtain High Court authentication, then obtain consular legalization from the destination jurisdiction's embassy or consulate; the document should include director signature pages and a witnessed English translation where required by the receiving authority.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Amended and Restated Memorandum and Articles of Association)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Approved by all founding shareholders and filed with the Hong Kong Companies Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: Notarize the certified copy of the registered Articles, then obtain an Apostille from the Hong Kong SAR High Court. Consular Legalization: Notarize, obtain Hong Kong High Court authentication, then present to the destination country's consular post for legalization where the destination is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The JV shareholder's or ultimate beneficial owner's relationship bank in the home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: Have the bank execute the letter, notarize the bank signatory's signature before a Hong Kong Notary Public or a local notary in the issuing country, and obtain an Apostille from the competent authority of the issuing state (Hong Kong High Court Registry; for mainland China, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or an authorized local Foreign Affairs Office). Consular Legalization: Where the banking institution is located in a non-Apostille state, follow the local notarization and judicial authentication chain, then consular-legalize at the destination state's consulate; a Hague Apostille must not be chained with a consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Individual UBO Declaration and Beneficial Ownership Structure Certificate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each ultimate beneficial owner, coordinated by incorporation counsel and certified by the company secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: Sign before a notary public and apostillize in the jurisdiction of the UBO's residence or passport (Hong Kong: High Court; mainland China: MFA or authorized local Foreign Affairs Office). Consular Legalization: For non-Apostille UBO jurisdictions, notarize, authenticate through the appropriate ministry or judicial authority, and then obtain consular legalization from the destination consulate; do not apply a Hague Apostille where consular legalization is the required route.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must be performed against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and Sectoral Sanctions Identifications, HKSAR sanctions lists published under the UN Sanctions Ordinance (Cap. 537), the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list, and the Mainland China unreliable entity list and foreign sanctions anti-boycott watchlist. The protocol must include a 14-point identity verification of all shareholders, directors, authorized signatories and actual controllers, with particular focus on politically exposed persons (PEPs) who are current or former senior officials, close associates and family members of Chinese mainland, Hong Kong and foreign public office holders. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is mandatory for any PEP, high-risk jurisdiction resident, sanctions-hit sector, or source-of-wealth opacity equal to or above the 25% UBO threshold; screening must be run at application onboarding, upon any rejection or adverse news, and within two business days of any transactional red flag, with results preserved for at least seven years under AMLO record-keeping requirements.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Hong Kong Companies Registry - Integrated Companies Registry Information System (ICRIS) online name search and e-Registry incorporation portal; for the mainland Chinese JV leg, the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System and the local Administration for Market Regulation enterprise name pre-approval platform.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Hong Kong permits an English name, a Chinese name, or both; the English name must end with 'Limited' and a Chinese name, if adopted, must end with the equivalent traditional Chinese limited-liability suffix. There is no mandatory four-tier name formula for Hong Kong, but the name must not be misleading, offensive, or identical to any other name on the Companies Registry register. For the mainland JV/WFOE leg, the registered Chinese name must comply with the PRC four-tier naming formula: administrative division plus distinctive trade name plus industry or operation category plus company type suffix; Pinyin transliteration is not acceptable as the registered Chinese name, and any English name for a mainland entity must be filed as a foreign-language trade name only if approved together with the Chinese name. Traditional and simplified Chinese characters are treated as equivalent for distinctiveness checks in mainland China, while the official mainland registered name must be in simplified Chinese.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon written refusal, the applicant must obtain the refusal notice stating the statutory ground. For Hong Kong, the applicant may request a review by the Companies Registry by filing a written application and supporting representation within 14 days and subsequently appeal to the Court of First Instance under the Companies Ordinance if the Registrar maintains the refusal. For the mainland leg, the applicant must file an administrative reconsideration with the local Administration for Market Regulation or the same-level people's government within 60 days of receiving the refusal, or alternatively initiate administrative litigation in the competent people's court within 6 months; counsel should simultaneously re-file a cleared alternative name to avoid delay and preserve the transaction timetable.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A Hong Kong registered office may be a physical address or the office of a licensed trust or company service provider, and a virtual office may satisfy the literal Companies Ordinance requirement if a real physical reception, mail-handling personnel and registered agent services are included. However, for the target industry of international bulk export of dried goji berries and herbal botanicals, the Inland Revenue Department and Hong Kong banks will generally reject a pure virtual mailbox for economic-substance and territorial-source-profit analysis. Banks under HKMA KYC standards require a physical operational address, named contact personnel, evidence of real procurement and warehousing contracts with Chinese suppliers, sample commercial contracts and supplier invoices; without these, account opening will be refused. For the mainland JV leg, a virtual office is not permissible; SAMR and the tax authority require a legal registered address matching the business license, an actual operating site, and customs and export registration with the same address for the herbal wholesale and export scope.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) review of registered office lease or rental invoice; (2) verification that the address is not a mere P.O. box or digital mailbox; (3) confirmation of on-site personnel, with at least one person performing administrative or sourcing activity; (4) presence of original supplier agreements, warehouse or logistics contracts, export records, customs declarations, and phytosanitary or health certificates for goji berry and herbal products; (5) telephone and on-site follow-up by the municipal tax bureau or Companies Registry upon mismatched filings; (6) unannounced inspections of mainland legal-person business premises by the local Administration for Market Regulation for foreign-invested enterprises in the import-export and food-herbal sector. Quantified risk: mainland leg 70% probability of an unannounced operational-site inspection within the first 24 months of incorporation because the entity will register for customs, tax and food or herbal export clearance; Hong Kong leg 25% probability of a physical inspection of the registered agent's office and 15% probability of an Inland Revenue Department field audit if the claimed principal place of operation is deemed inconsistent with the registered office address.
